analysis:
The only change in SSDPrefixCache.swift is in retireIndexedEntries (patch hunk around head lines 1794-1800, outside the supplied excerpts). Previously one removalLock hold covered the whole batch of URLs. Now SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.removeInSlices(urls) runs a closure per slice, and each slice takes removalLock separately and still checks hasSafeRoot and ownsEvictionRoot before calling SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.remove with root, index and epochStore. The safety guards (safe root, epoch ownership) are preserved per slice. The closure returns nil when a guard fails, and removeInSlices must handle nil.

Security-relevant behavior I checked: (1) TTL sweep and eviction (sweepExpiredEntries, lines in base 1848-1855) still go through retireIndexedEntries, so the TTL bound in T-041(b) is unchanged. (2) Releasing the lock between slices lets a successor or close() change ownership mid-batch. Each later slice re-evaluates ownsEvictionRoot, so it refuses to touch a successor's files. (3) Atomicity across slices is lost, so a partial removal is possible. Index reconciliation via reconcileExternalRemovals still runs if externalChange is set; this depends on how removeInSlices merges results.

Not visible: the implementation of removeInSlices (slice size, nil handling, result merging, externalChange aggregation). This is outside the supplied evidence, so I record it as an unverified contract, not a finding. The rest of the file is unchanged context: scanOnDisk symlink and fanout checks, settleDurableDonation verification, and staging and ticket accounting. The visible head lines 1-655 are unchanged. I identified no new regression to T-041, A-001 or the at-rest crypto, HMAC naming and KEK-wipe mitigations. The next pass should check removeInSlices in SSDOwnedEntryRetirement for correct nil-result handling, result merging and slice bounds.
